situation.summary: Move-out defect works at vacant 46 Fernwick Lane, following a check-out report (A1). The contractor, Alderwick Property Works, sent a single lump-sum quote of £3,865.68 on 15 Sep (A2, E013). Maya Chen forwarded it to the landlord, Owen Vale, at 13:53 and asked whether he was happy to proceed (E014). The system flagged that the amount is above the approval threshold and that landlord approval is required (E015). At 16:25 the landlord call reached no substantive outcome (E017), so there is no approval, no instruction and no attendance date. The quote has no per-item prices, VAT basis or exclusions, and it does not cover several checkout items (carpets, kitchen flooring, laminate repair, curtain pole, curtains and bulbs, boiler inspection, kitchen worktop, and the other radiators).
situation.task: Before the landlord decides on the £3,865.68 lump sum, get an itemised price, VAT basis and exclusions from the contractor, and put the omitted checkout items to the landlord.
situation.stageLabel: Quote received; awaiting landlord approval of £3,865.68 lump-sum move-out works (approval not given; scope and VAT basis unclear)
situation.whoseMove: Owen Vale (landlord) must approve or reject the lump sum. His reply is not yet due: the ask went out at 13:53 on 15 Sep, no date was given, and the usual gap is about 3 days, so a chase is not due until Thu 18 Sep. Our move now, before he decides: (1) email Iris Bell (Alderwick) asking for a per-task price, VAT basis and exclusions against the checkout report, the report version she priced from, whether an inspection is needed, and confirming that no work is approved and nothing should be booked yet, followUpBy Wed 17 Sep; (2) alsoSend Owen Vale by email a short scope note naming the omitted items, the boiler casing and the non-working smoke detector, asking whether to add the omitted items or leave them, and saying we will send the itemised figures by Wed 17 Sep. Then case.wait; if he is silent, chase by email and phone on Thu 18 Sep.

decision.message:
Dear Iris,

Re: 46 Fernwick Lane, Aldermead – quotation NBL-027-Q1 (15 September 2025), £3,865.68

Thank you for the quotation. I have sent it to the landlord. Before he can decide, I need a few more details:

1. A price for each task listed (newel post, door frame, uPVC window frame holes, wall damage, threshold, toilet-roll holder, smoke detector, rehanging the kitchen radiator, each of the two extractor fans, en-suite radiator, ceiling stain-blocking, decoration), rather than one "Labour & Materials" figure.
2. The VAT basis. Does £3,865.68 include VAT, is VAT to be added, or are you not VAT-registered?
3. Please confirm that the two "renew an extractor fan" lines are two separate fans.
4. What the quote excludes. The check-out report also lists replacement carpets (quote requested), kitchen flooring damage, chipped living-room laminate, the bedroom curtain pole, curtains and bulbs, the warped kitchen worktop, the boiler casing, and rusting radiators other than the en-suite. Please say whether any of these are included. If you can price any of them, please list them separately.
5. Please confirm which check-out report you priced from (reference NBL-027-CHECKOUT, the current report) and whether you need to inspect before work starts. If you do, keys can be collected from our office.

Please note that the landlord has not approved this quote or any works yet, even though our original job email suggested otherwise. Please do not book or start any work until we confirm his approval in writing.

Could you reply by Wednesday 17 September? If anything is unclear, please call me.

Kind regards,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The quote went to the landlord at 13:53 today (E014). The call at 16:25 did not reach him (E017). It is too soon to chase him, since a chase is usually about 3 days after the ask. The quote itself is not enough for a firm approval. It is one lump sum with no task prices, VAT basis or exclusions (E013, A2). It also leaves out several items from the check-out report (A1). The rules say to settle price and scope before the visit and to always state the VAT basis. These are new questions for the contractor, not a repeat of an earlier ask, so they can go now. The contractor was also told the works had been agreed with the landlord (E004), but the system records that approval is still needed (E015). That has to be corrected before she books anything. Who controls scope is a landlord matter, so the landlord gets a scope note in alsoSend with a date for the itemised figures.
decision.expectedOutcome: By 17 Sep the contractor sends an itemised quote with the VAT basis and exclusions, and confirms she will not book until approval is given. The landlord knows about the scope gaps and can decide which items to add before approving.
boundaries: Asking for itemisation does not approve the quote or any works.
The landlord has not approved £3,865.68 or any scope.
This does not decide who pays for any item. Any recharge to the outgoing tenant needs check-in evidence.
No safety assessment of the boiler casing or the ceiling water damage is made or implied.
remainingWork: Send the itemised quote and VAT basis to the landlord once received.
Chase the landlord on Thu 18 Sep by phone and email if there is no decision.
Get prices for any omitted items the landlord wants added.

alsoSend.message:
Dear Owen,

Re: 46 Fernwick Lane – move-out works quotation, £3,865.68

I tried to call you this afternoon but couldn't get through. Following my earlier email, I have asked the contractor to break the £3,865.68 down by task, to confirm whether VAT is included or added, and to list anything that is excluded. I will send you this by Wednesday 17 September.

Please be aware that the quote does not cover these items from the check-out report:
- replacement carpets (a quote was requested)
- kitchen flooring damage and the chipped living-room laminate
- bedroom curtain pole, curtains and bulbs
- the warped kitchen worktop with reported water ingress
- rusting radiators other than the en-suite
- the boiler casing, which appears to be held with tape and was noted as needing inspection

Could you let me know which of these you would like us to add or get priced, and which you would rather leave or arrange yourself? Please let me know whether you would like a qualified engineer to inspect the boiler. That decision is yours. The quote does include renewing the non-working top-floor smoke detector.

No works have been approved or booked. Nothing will go ahead until you confirm in writing, against a firm figure.

Kind regards,
Maya Chen
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings

issues.claim: The landlord email says the call 'couldn't get through', but E017 records an automated recording notice and an unclear utterance. The call may have reached voicemail or a person, so 'couldn't get through' overstates what the record shows.
issues.suggestion: Reword to 'I tried to call you this afternoon and was unable to speak with you'.

issues.claim: The landlord email promises to send the itemised breakdown 'by Wednesday 17 September'. That date depends on the contractor replying, and she has not confirmed it. She has also been slow to respond (E006–E012).
issues.suggestion: Say 'I have asked the contractor to reply by Wednesday 17 September and will forward it as soon as I have it'.
